Description: At the Entrance, the visitor clashes with the residents over identity confirmation. The inviter’s identity is explicitly denied, and under pressure from the severe weather, the visitor is allowed into the villa.
Location: Entrance (Entrance)
Key Information:
  - The events take place at the villa Entrance (Entrance).
  - When the door first opens, a resident is clearly drunk or emotionally unstable and cannot provide useful information.
  - The visitor clearly states that he came because of an invitation and is looking for Mr. Rupert Galley.
  - After some time, the door is opened again.
  - Edmund Galley (Eddie) denies knowing the visitor and denies having sent an invitation.
  - Edmund Galley clearly states that he has lived here for a long time and has never heard of Rupert Galley.
  - The visitor’s vehicle is stuck in the muddy road near Quail Lane (Quail Lane), preventing him from leaving immediately.
  - An item falls and shatters near the doorway; Edmund Galley judges it to be a doll from inside the house.
  - After seeing the severe weather, Victoria Maseko (Vic) opposes driving the visitor away.
  - The final decision is to let the visitor into the villa; the other residents are in the Living room (Living room).
  - Edmund Galley warns that a woman inside is emotionally unstable and could cause serious consequences.
Characters:
  [John Hobbes (John Hobbes)] Person No. 1, the visitor.
    · States that he came because of an invitation and is looking for Mr. Galley.
    · Explains that his car is stuck near Quail Lane (Quail Lane), making him late and unable to leave immediately.
    · Continues trying to explain his purpose after being refused.
    · Accepts the arrangement to enter the villa after persuasion from others.
  [Person No. 10] One of the residents who initially opens the door.
    · Appears clearly drunk or emotionally unstable.
    · Cannot sustain a conversation and leaves midway.
    · Mentions the name Harry Thornton without explanation.
  [Edmund Galley (Eddie Galley)] Person No. 6, one of the villa residents.
    · Denies knowing the visitor and denies having sent an invitation.
    · Clearly states that he has never heard of Rupert Galley.
    · Initially insists on keeping the visitor out.
    · Judges the shattered item in the Entrance to be a doll from inside the house.
    · Warns that a woman inside is emotionally unstable and could cause serious consequences.
  [Victoria Maseko (Vic)] Person No. 7, one of the villa residents.
    · Notices the severe weather outside and opposes driving the visitor away immediately.
    · Argues to let the visitor inside first and resolve the issue afterward.
    · Informs the visitor that the others are currently in the Living room (Living room).
  [Rupert Galley] The inviter’s name shown on the invitation.
    · Identified by the visitor as the inviter.
    · Explicitly denied by Edmund Galley as someone who exists among the villa’s residents or acquaintances.
